compounding_issues: Every session (1-5) aborted with the same infrastructure failure ('Unexpected server error', exit code 1) at ~2s, so no session produced any code — the story never actually started.
The runner kept attempting 5 sessions instead of aborting after the first identical backend error, compounding a single infrastructure failure into five wasted attempts.
Each 'session' commit contains nothing but a `.instrument/session_N.jsonl` error log line; the commits are empty shells that do not build on each other.
No pre-flight validation of the model backend was performed, so the run burned the full story slot (10.4s, 5 commits) on a known-dead execution path.
key_decisions: Seed codebase: single-file Flask + sqlite3 task manager with clean seams (models/routes/error handling) — the intended foundation, never built upon.
Instrumentation design: per-session error logs written to `.instrument/session_*.jsonl` and committed as the session artifact, which is what the five '[story]' commits actually contain.
No code-writing agent ever ran: 0 tokens, 0 tool calls, 0 tests, 0 files created across all sessions (deepseek-v4-pro, clean condition).
story_review.trajectory_description: Quality was flat at zero across the entire arc. Sessions 1 through 5 are indistinguishable: each produced the same immediate server-error, zero-token failure and committed only its own error-log line. There is no code evolution, no compounding of engineering decisions, and no final deliverable — the trajectory is a horizontal line of identical infrastructure failures rather than an improving or degrading build.
story_review.summary: This is a failed run, not a story: the model backend died on every session (0 tokens, exit code 1 each), leaving five empty error-log commits and an untouched seed app, so the intended greenfield→feature→integration→refactor→cross-cutting progression was never realized.
